newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran stages war games near Afghanistan border.
newsitem.headline: Iran stages war games near Afghanistan border.

text.p: Iranian forces have launched war games near the Afghanistan border, a major drug smuggling route, a Tehran newspaper said on Wednesday.
The daily Kayhan said army forces using "advanced weapons" were staging the manoeuvres near Torbat-e Jam, about 60 km (38 miles) from the Afghan border. It did not say when the exercises began.
An army commander said about 70 senior officers were monitoring the manoeuvres held to enhance the combat readiness of the Iranian forces, it said.
Iran has been building up its defences along its eastern borders to stop drug smuggling, particularly since the Taleban Afghan militia gained control over areas across the border.

Shi'ite Islamic Iran has accused the militant Sunni Taleban of giving Islam a bad name and refused to recognise the Taleban government. It has backed the ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani as the legitimate Afghan head of state.
Iranian media have accused the Taleban of profiting from the drug trade and supporting armed smugglers, a charge Taleban officials have denied.
Iran is a key transit route for drugs, mostly opium from which heroin is made, being smuggled to Europe via Turkey from Afghanistan and Pakistan -- the so-called "Golden Crescent".
Tehran has said police seized 175 tonnes of drugs in the Iranian year which ended on March 20.
